notes: Conditional two-income-state response: at date0 baseline is node11 and adverse realization node10; thereafter original transitions resume.
Same future inverse-CDF uniform draws across arms and models; these are coupled discrete Markov innovations, not identical additive AR innovations.
Fiscal implementation shocks are identical across both arms and Fiscal models; Ramsey has none in its original solution.
Each debt scenario inherits the exact debt node from sampled stationary Ramsey predecessor histories with prior income node11. Both arms use the SAME pre-shock history and successor-price menu.
Ramsey does not reoptimize its initial promised price when the shock arrives. Subsequent promises use saved continuation menus.
Requested debt targets are rounded to adjacent feasible saved debt nodes; actual values and history counts are reported.
Reputation conditions on a permanently strategic government; initial priors are reported separately. These beliefs describe a learning transition, not its asymptotic posterior.
Flow responses are percentages of FIXED pre-shock quarterly income, avoiding denominator artifacts. Debt reference scaling uses four times that income.
Primary balance=y-c=kappa*b-q*(bp-(1-delta)*b). No separate tax or government-spending instruments exist.
Spreads are quarterly basis points. Monte Carlo SE is simulation error, not empirical or parameter uncertainty.
Ramsey selected histories satisfy previous income and issued-debt conditions; impacts average over inherited promise heterogeneity.
Only government beta changes from annual 0.90 to 0.85; lender rate, rule, grids, and all other primitives match the original snapshot. All three equilibria are newly solved.

The lower-beta stationary Ramsey history simulation uses eight million periods because the lowest original debt node had only thirteen qualifying histories in the first million. Initial debt nodes and conditional-history criteria are unchanged.

ramsey_solver.solver_note: Howard20 cycled at beta annual0.85; unaccelerated Bellman iteration used with unchanged convergence tolerance.
